summary.hostile_goal: Installer has seven distinct supported hostile findings; no quota-driven additions or removals.
summary.validation: Run make validate as the final task action; final response supplies its result.

changes.reason: Existing agent findings described Python and PowerShell tasks. Follow Assembly.Load receiver provenance through GetType/GetMethod to an actual invocation; ordinary managed plugin hosts remain neutral.

limitations: Each BENIGN judgment concerns the listed source/template as packaged, after inspecting its implemented actions. It is not an authorization finding for a deployment, and it does not downgrade accurate attack capabilities.
The supplied archive convictions were retained without re-judging them or using them to convict members. Package authenticity and operational deployment were not independently established.

The model bundle warns that v18 features lag the v21 engine schema. Gate=FLAGGED means atomscan admitted the artifact; gate=BENIGN means it did not. Raw probabilities and calibrated levels are retained per sample.

Initial scans inherited follow-all settings and included retrieved reference material, so controlled before/after comparisons use identical no-follow options against the baseline trait snapshot and the edited tree.

Warm native analysis returned different Mach-O slice facts. Cache-disabled scans of both rule sets agree exactly: standalone native analysis selects ARM64; the installer inside its archive contributes x86-64 facts. Both slices contain the same recovered AppleScript. No YAML detection was weakened to accommodate that scanner/cache variance.

Python flow is source-local may-flow, not runtime reachability; nested-function producer limitations prevent this neutral invocation matcher from covering every background-thread path. The non-nested csharp_exe path is matched.

The legacy regression checker has six baseline failures, including retired cradle/dispatch/socket IDs and existing SMB packet fixture misses. All 57 observed finding populations are unchanged by this task.

samples.name: Installer
samples.marker_note: Installer stealer: phishes and exports secrets; attack traits retained
samples.evidence: ARM64 entry decrypts a 37077-byte command, converts it to a C++ string and passes it to system. XOR uses seed 0x11667 and uint32(state*0x3785) modulo 35999; the same command exists in the x86 slice. The decoded osascript program validates a hidden password prompt using dscl, stages browser/wallet/keychain/Notes/document data, creates a ZIP, uploads it and removes staging. It also replaces Ledger Live from a remote ZIP and installs a KeepAlive/RunAtLoad system LaunchDaemon. UserName selects the current user, so root execution is not inferred merely from privileged installation.
samples.context_limit: No installation history, downstream payload or runtime success is established.
samples.verdict_basis: Concealed broad secret collection, validated credential phishing, export and application replacement contradict installer purpose.
